why_no_successor_package: A successor package can change a line's dollars with the operations core v85 already has. It cannot emit the Form 8949 row Example 2 requires. Building a core that only zeros column (h) would miss the charter.

attempts.change: On attachment-rule.v11, an adjustment row of a published kind may list enumerate_published. The sign stays negative and the kind stays closed.

cause: Form 8949 rows in this product are recorded family members. Code W and code B each have a family, and the attachment itemizes that family's proceeds, basis, and adjustment under a fixed label. collect_members has no filter. Adjustment kinds on the published attachment schemas are nominee, accrued interest, and ABP, and the sign is fixed negative. A v11 adjustment row of one of those kinds may list enumerate_published, and that fragment validates, but the collector emits one value per finding and the sign is still negative. Positive itemization rows on v11 still require collect_members. A subject rule can publish the code L amount, and a line rule can add it, but neither produces columns (d), (e), (f), (g), and (h) for that sale, and a covered loss stays in the line 1a or 8a family.
smallest_change: A recording-surface change, then content only. When box 7 is yes and column (h) before code L is negative, record that sale in a code L family the way a code B sale is recorded, with proceeds, the basis shown, and the code L amount computed from those amounts and any wash or code B adjustment already recorded. A successor attachment itemizes it, and the successor Schedule D lines pick up column (h), which the instructions put at zero. No new filer amount, no kernel change, and no edit of a published schema. The other sufficient change is a new attachment schema that can itemize one derived sale as columns (d) through (h) and a line rule that can drop that sale from line 1a or 8a. That is a schema and a presentation change.
